review_iterations.preliminary_findings: Before formal READY/verdict, reviewed session expiry and disabled mandatory identity edge. Disabled-before-name correction and regression were delivered after READY but before first formal verdict. No defect or fix cycle is hidden by the lack of an earlier verdict. During final review, Orchestrator highlighted naive datetime-object setter semantics; Reviewer reproduced immediate fresh-session data loss and rejects iteration 1 pending fix.

comments.text: set_session coerces a legacy naive datetime created_at through _timestamp(), attaching UTC rather than interpreting local time. On UTC+3, await set_session(1,{"mode":"it_support","created_at":datetime.now()}); await get_session(1) immediately loses mode because the new timestamp appears in the future. Original setter preserved naive local isoformat semantics. Normalize naive created_at datetime objects as local time (consistently with legacy naive strings), preserve aware UTC, and add regression for fresh and expired datetime-object input.

Documented operational risk: event locks serialize only within one process; Redis get/set is not an atomic cross-pod ticket claim. active_ticket_uuid is available, but future ticket wiring must not claim distributed deduplication. Memory fallback is explicitly local. Synchronous Redis I/O has 5s timeouts; latency AC remain unverified.

The existing orchestrator llm_requests_total collector is correctly reused through a bounded facade, with success|failure matching its exporter. Direct writes through the existing exporter bypass the facade. Future wiring must avoid unbounded provider names and duplicate/inconsistent accounting between observers and exporter snapshots; no protected exporter monkeypatch is introduced.
